chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

While a man is behind the Qa'im (the Awaited One), ordering and forbidding, he (the Qa'im) orders that his neck be struck (killed). Then nothing between the two horizons remains but that it fears him.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Mahdi in Shia eschatology
key_terms.بَيْنَ الْخَافِقَيْنِ: Between the two horizons, meaning the entire world
key_terms.ضَرْبِ الْعُنُقِ: Striking the neck, a method of execution or killing

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the man standing behind al-Qa'im in this hadith?
ai.summary: In the Nu'mani tradition, this narration highlights the absolute authority of al-Qa'im, where even his immediate attendants are subject to his decisive command, illustrating the totality of his rule. The phrase 'between the two horizons' (bayna al-khafayqayn) signifies the entire inhabited world, emphasizing that his sovereignty will inspire universal awe and submission. This reflects the Shia eschatological view of the Mahdi as the ultimate just ruler whose presence commands reverence from all creation.
